title: Personal Training Packages: how an active club membership shortens the tenure required for the loyalty bonus session
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Personal Training Packages product line and states the tenure basis, and the club-membership acceleration to it, for the complimentary loyalty bonus session.

## Rule
A package must have been opened at least 7 calendar days before the current moment, counted as full calendar days from the purchase date with no partial-day rounding, before its loyalty bonus session is owed. Where the member's own club membership is active, that membership's own personal-training discount percentage reduces this 7-day requirement proportionally as a loyalty acceleration: the 7-day requirement is scaled down to the fraction that remains once that percentage is set aside, and only that single scaled figure is then rounded down to the nearest whole day. Where no active club membership is held, the full 7-day requirement applies with no reduction.

## Points of judgement
- What is held: an active club membership.
- What value it contributes: that membership's own personal-training discount percentage.
- What effect it has: the 7-day requirement is scaled down by the remaining fraction after that percentage is set aside, and the single rounding-down step is applied only to that final scaled figure -- never to a discount amount worked out and rounded down on its own beforehand; the requirement never lengthens and never goes below zero days.
As a hypothetical illustration only, if the linked active membership's own personal-training discount percentage were 20, the remaining fraction of the requirement would be 80 percent, and the 7-day requirement scaled to that remaining fraction comes to 5.6 days; rounding that single scaled figure down to the nearest whole day gives a requirement of 5 days. A package that has been open for at least that (possibly reduced) number of full calendar days meets this tenure condition; a package open for fewer full calendar days than that does not.

## Correct reading versus a common misreading
Misreading: working out the discount amount on the 7-day requirement by itself (20 percent of 7 days is 1.4 days), rounding that discount amount down on its own (to 1 day), and only then subtracting that already-rounded amount from the 7-day requirement. This is not the basis this policy uses, and it diverges from the correct basis whenever the discount amount by itself is not already a whole number of days.
Correct basis: the discount percentage is applied to the full 7-day requirement first, producing one combined scaled figure, and the single rounding-down step falls only on that combined figure -- never on an intermediate discount amount computed and rounded down separately.
